New stability record for Italy's Meloni may prove fleeting
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-31
07:36:04 UTC
16:36:04 KST

New stability record for Italy's Meloni may prove fleeting
ROME, Aug 31 - In a country famed for political instability, Giorgia Meloni is poised to lead Italy's longest-lasting government since World War Two, overtaking a record of 1,412 consecutive days set by Silvio Berlusconi in 2005.
Meloni, who has tempered her populist instincts with pragmatism since taking power in October 2022, plans a rally on Friday, September 4 to celebrate the milestone, framing the durability of her coalition as one of its crowning achievements.
After cycling through 68 governments in 80 years, Italy has proved much steadier during a period of global conflict than France, which has had five prime ministers since the autumn of 2022, while Britain has got through four.
But just as Italy has shaken off its reputation for volatility, opinion polls suggest that the 2027 parliamentary elections could usher in a more fragmented and potentially less stable political landscape.
"There is a genuine risk that we could return to the worst kind of a splintered parliament next time around," said Roberto D'Alimonte, a professor of Italian politics at Rome's Luiss university.
While Berlusconi's single-term record is about to be eclipsed, he will remain the longest-serving Italian prime minister overall, with a tenure of about nine years over four terms between 1994 and 2011.
BUDGET DISCIPLINE
Worried about the prospect of renewed political turbulence, coalition allies are quick to tout the dividends of four years of uninterrupted rule.
Deputy Foreign Minister Edmondo Cirielli, of Meloni's Brothers of Italy party, said the government had kept deficits and debt under control, while adding 1.2 million workers to the jobs market, pushing unemployment to under 6%.
"The record figures on employment and unemployment are indisputable," he told Reuters.
Analysts broadly agree that Meloni's strongest achievement has been restoring confidence in Italy's shaky public finances, blighted by a hefty debt mountain.
Lorenzo Codogno, a former chief economist at the Treasury and now head of LC Macro Advisors, said the cabinet had convinced investors it was committed to budget discipline and had curtailed costly policies of past administrations, notably the "Superbonus" home renovation scheme.
"In terms of fiscal responsibility, I think the government has done a decent job. In terms of promoting growth and reforming the economy, not much has been done," he said.
Little effort was made to shake up an inefficient public administration, the health service and education system, while all the government's institutional reforms, including handing more powers to the prime minister, have floundered.
"Part of the reason Meloni has been able to stay in power for four years is that she did not try to change much or upset voters," said Lorenzo Pregliasco, head of YouTrend pollster.
"This is perhaps the most sobering lesson we can draw from this period."
LOSING TRUMP
While ducking ambitious change, Meloni focused on law and order, boosting police powers and cracking down on irregular immigration — a key electoral pledge — cutting the number of new arrivals to 66,316 last year from 157,651 in 2023.
"There has been the paradigm shift imposed by Giorgia Meloni in the management of illegal immigration," Francesco Filini, the head of Brothers of Italy's policy programme, told Reuters, saying much of Europe was now looking to emulate her.
Although she has forged good relations with many European leaders, Meloni's standing abroad has been bruised by the collapse of her once-close ties with Donald Trump after the U.S. president accused her in April of lacking courage and letting the United States down in its war with Iran.
The diplomatic setback, which destroyed any pretence that Meloni could serve as a bridge between Europe and Washington, came within weeks of a stinging domestic defeat, when Italians rejected her flagship judicial reform in a referendum.
The loss punctured the aura of invincibility that had surrounded Meloni's coalition, and while her party remains the most popular in Italy, the standing of her main allies — most notably the far-right League — has dropped steadily.
With time running out, the government has embarked on one last-gasp legislative push, seeking to redraw the electoral law by introducing a system that would give a majority bonus to any bloc winning more than 42% of the vote.
Critics say the change is designed to strengthen the conservative bloc's chances of staying in power. Meloni says it is aimed at providing renewed stability, whoever wins.
NEW PARTY DISRUPTS OUTLOOK
However, the political landscape has changed since the law was devised, thanks to the emergence of a new far-right party led by an ex-general, Roberto Vannacci, who has tapped into anxieties over immigration, security and cultural change with language that is markedly blunter than Meloni's.
A poll published by BiDiMedia on August 26 put the coalition partners on just 38.5%, while the broad centre-left camp, which is deeply divided over foreign policy and prone to relentless infighting, is hovering close to the vital 42% threshold.
Support for Vannacci has surged to 8%, suggesting he could win it for Meloni, if she agreed to bring him into her alliance.
That would be a risky move which might alienate moderate voters and alarm EU allies concerned by Vannacci's extremism. Alternatively, she could hope for an inconclusive vote and seek a post-election pact with Vannacci to give her a working majority.
Either way, the path to another stable government appears narrower than before. The opposition is disunited, while Vannacci's rise risks turning a previously disciplined conservative alliance into a more fractious bloc.
"The markets have liked stability and got used to it, but this is Italy, it won't last for ever," said Codogno. REUTERS

Italy's revolving-door governments — the numbers behind the instability
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-31
07:35:51 UTC
16:35:51 KST

Italy's revolving-door governments — the numbers behind the instability
ROME, Aug 31 - Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni is due to set a record as leading Italy's longest-serving administration on September 4. Yet the country's revolving-door cabinets have often masked a more stable political system than first meets the eye.
Below are some facts and figures about Italy's post-war governments:
HOW MANY GOVERNMENTS AND PRIME MINISTERS?
Meloni's administration is Italy's 68th government since 1946, led by the country's 31st prime minister of the republican era. Unlike in some countries, a new government is said to have been created after a major cabinet reshuffle, even if the prime minister remains the same.
AVERAGE LIFESPAN
Across the 80 years from the formation of Alcide De Gasperi's government in July 1946 to Meloni's record in 2026, the average cabinet has lasted roughly 14 months. The figure varies according to methodology: calculating only the period from a government's swearing-in to its resignation produces a shorter average, because outgoing cabinets often remain in office in a caretaker capacity.
THE SHORTEST AND THE LONGEST
The briefest tenure was Amintore Fanfani's first government, which lasted 22 days in 1954. Before Meloni, only four administrations lasted more than 1,000 days: Silvio Berlusconi's 2nd government (1,412 days, from 2001 to 2005), Berlusconi's 4th government (1,287 days, 2008 to 2011), Bettino Craxi (1,093 days, 1983 to 1986) and Matteo Renzi (1,024 days, 2014 to 2016). Altogether, Berlusconi served about nine years over four terms.
WHY SO MANY SHORT-LIVED GOVERNMENTS?
Italy's post-war system combined proportional representation, which encouraged a fragmented party landscape, with coalition governments vulnerable to disputes. The constitution also requires a government to retain the confidence of both the lower house and the Senate — two houses with equal powers, giving small coalition partners considerable leverage.
However, the turnover did not always mean a wholesale change of political direction. During much of the post-war era, the Christian Democrats remained at the centre of power, while prime ministers and coalition formulas revolved around them.
Despite frequent changes of government, nine of Italy's 18 post-war legislatures ran broadly to the end of their normal five-year term, while five lasted for four years.
ELECTORAL LAWS: A FREQUENTLY CHANGING RULEBOOK
Italy has deployed three different electoral systems in general elections in the past 22 years, with Meloni promising to introduce a fourth ahead of the 2027 vote, saying it will bring greater stability. REUTERS

Feature: How World Heritage bid breathes new life into a Chinese village
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-31
15:31:07 CST
16:31:07 KST

NANCHANG, Aug. 31 (Xinhua) -- On a sultry afternoon, an elderly man sat on the doorstep of his home in Dongbu Village, a riverside settlement about 40 kilometers from Jingdezhen, idly fanning himself in the shade when a visiting official stopped to ask him a question.
"Do you know what big thing your village is doing these days?"
Without a word, he turned the fan in his hand. Printed across its face was a single line: "Supporting the World Heritage bid."
"That's it," he said, "We're applying for World Heritage status."
Everyone laughed. For Han Xiaoshan, deputy director of the World Heritage application office in Fuliang County, where the village sits, the moment was proof that years of knocking on doors had finally sunk in.
"It showed our work hadn't been for nothing," she said. "People here know now that this is everyone's business, not just ours."
It had taken years to get there -- years of persuading villagers to look again at the street, houses and riverfront they had grown up with, and to see not just a familiar home, but a piece of porcelain history worth preserving.
On July 25, the Jingdezhen Handicraft Porcelain Industry Sites were inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List, becoming China's 61st World Heritage site. Dongbu was among the newly listed heritage components.
For centuries, kaolin, or China clay, and other porcelain-making materials were brought down from the surrounding hills to Dongbu and shipped along the Donghe River to Jingdezhen's kilns. Goods purchased in the porcelain-making city traveled back along the same route.
With an ancient trade route also running through the village, Dongbu became a busy hub for trade and transshipment by land and water. Its old wharf, commercial street and waterways still trace the transport network that once helped supply Jingdezhen's porcelain industry.
For generations of villagers, however, those remains were simply part of everyday life.
Wu Jinghua, a former village official who has lived in Dongbu for more than 70 years, remembers efforts to protect the old street and wharf beginning around 2000. Systematic restoration gathered pace from 2015 as the World Heritage application moved forward.
Dongbu was traditionally an agricultural village. Tourism developed gradually, but few visitors came at first.
As heritage protection intensified, it began to affect residents more directly. Concrete covering the old stone street had to be removed, old houses faced restrictions on rebuilding and renovation, and makeshift structures and accumulated clutter had to be cleared.
For some villagers, the changes initially meant inconvenience rather than opportunity.
"At first, many villagers did not understand," Wu said. "Old houses were too dilapidated to be worth preserving."
For Han, who joined the application effort in 2022, changing that perception became part of the work.
She and her colleagues went door to door, explaining Dongbu's history and why the old streets and wharf outside villagers' homes mattered beyond the village itself.
Gradually, resistance eased. As the village became cleaner and its historic buildings were repaired, Han said, residents developed a stronger sense of belonging and pride.
The restoration itself followed a principle of "minimum intervention."
Traditional materials and techniques were used to repair old buildings, the wharf and the stone-paved street, with colors and textures kept as close as possible to the originals.
When workers moved utility lines underground, they marked each stone slab before lifting it. Once the work was complete, workers returned the slabs one by one to their original positions. Modern shop windows were replaced with wooden latticework to better match the historic streetscape.
At the same time, the village upgraded water and drainage systems and improved other basic infrastructure.
The changes also created new opportunities for residents.
More than 80 villagers found work during the restoration projects. Others opened homestays, restaurants and teahouses or began selling local produce to visitors.
Under a large banyan tree by the Donghe River, one elderly resident now sells mung bean soup and rice jelly, often going through two buckets a day.
Dongbu has also begun hosting study tours and cultural tourism programs centered on its role in Jingdezhen's porcelain history.
The village now receives at least 190,000 visitors a year, according to Wu. More visitors mean more customers for local food, accommodation and produce, giving villagers additional ways to earn a living beyond farming.
But another change is harder to measure.
The old houses that some villagers once saw mainly as dilapidated structures have increasingly become a source of pride. A history long taken for granted has become more closely tied to how residents see their home.
"This village isn't just our own place anymore," Wu said. "It now has international influence."
For Dongbu, World Heritage status has changed not only how its old street and wharf are protected, but also how residents understand their value.
"We all have the same hope now: to protect our ancient street and wharf well, so that our culture can be passed down for generations," said Wu. ■

Feature: Fresh banana exports to China lift incomes in NW Cambodia's border province
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-31
15:30:58 CST
16:30:58 KST

Workers wash fresh bananas at the packing factory of a Chinese-invested banana farm in Oddar Meanchey province, Cambodia on Aug. 30, 2026. (Photo by Van Pov/Xinhua)
ODDAR MEANCHEY, Cambodia, Aug. 31 (Xinhua) -- Lak Sineth, a 29-year-old single mother in Cambodia's northwestern Oddar Meanchey province, has seen her livelihood transformed since she began working at a local banana plantation in 2022.
The plantation, operated by Longfruiter Anlong Veng Oddar Meanchey Agriculture Park Co., Ltd., is close to the border with Thailand. The company currently cultivates the yellow Cavendish banana variety across roughly 530 hectares in the Anlong Veng district, providing steady employment for more than 800 residents.
Now a banana packing team leader, Sineth recalls starting with next to nothing. Her steady income has since allowed her to secure a baseline of financial stability and invest in her future.
"After coming to work at this banana plantation, I could afford my own land and other valuable possessions," Sineth told Xinhua on Sunday. "My life has been much better than before."
Cheat Chumpou, a 24-year-old banana washer, shared a similar perspective. Ever since she joined the factory, her financial situation has improved significantly thanks to the stable wages and supportive environment.
Before securing this job, Chumpou lived with her parents, who are farmers. She recalled that their livelihood was incredibly difficult, and they frequently lived hand-to-mouth.
"I want to thank the Chinese investors for investing in Cambodia," she said. "It has created many jobs and made life much better for Cambodian people."
Oeun Samkeary, the factory's 30-year-old production manager, noted that this yellow banana is a unique variety in Cambodia, standing out for its superior quality and taste compared to local options.
Samkeary added that the company's export volumes to China have grown steadily. Shipments rose from 24,000 tonnes in 2024 to more than 34,000 tonnes in 2025. So far in 2026, the company has already exported 22,000 tonnes to the Chinese market.
"Looking ahead for the rest of 2026, I think exports will keep rising due to growing demand and our newly expanded cultivation area in Cambodia," he said. "The cultivation of this yellow banana and its direct export to China have generated income for local people through job creation."
Cambodia's yellow banana exports have maintained vigorous momentum since 2019, when China first permitted direct shipments from the country.
Thong Mengdavid, deputy director of the China-ASEAN Studies Center at the Cambodia University of Technology and Science, said that China serves as the primary growth engine for Cambodia's commercial banana industry, absorbing roughly 95 percent of the country's total fresh yellow banana exports.
"Access to China's massive consumer base has transformed local banana farming into a modern, export-driven agribusiness," he told Xinhua. "This generates stable year-round employment, facilitates technology transfers, and upgrades infrastructure for thousands of rural farming communities."
Yellow bananas are among five Cambodian fresh fruits that currently enjoy direct access to the Chinese market, alongside mangoes, Pailin longans, coconuts, and durians. ■

The City as a System of Health: Breaking Feedback Loops in Planning
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-31
07:30:00 UTC
16:30:00 KST

The spatial consequences of urban form are revealed when health outcomes are mapped over neighborhoods. Neighborhoods that support walking, daily errands, social interaction, and access to essential services create opportunities to incorporate physical activity into routine tasks. Places that are organized around long distances and automobile travel suppress this opportunity. Physical activity and the motivation to incorporate it into daily life are shaped by the distance to a grocery store, the safety of a pedestrian crossing, the frequency of public transportation, the width of a sidewalk, and the quantity of services within walking distance.
For decades, conversations about rising obesity and metabolic health have concentrated on individual behavior. People are encouraged to exercise more, eat better, and make healthier choices. Good urban design practices challenge the environment that makes these practical and accessible. Consider a neighborhood where the nearest grocery store is several miles away, the streets are wide with high travel speeds, sidewalks are intermittent, and services between are dispersed. Driving is the rational response for this specific task of reaching the grocery store. Walking requires additional time, exposure to traffic and unsafe sidewalk conditions, or routes that don't offer safety or shade. Repeated across millions of daily trips, these ordinary choices influence how people move through their environments.

AI generated
JERUSALEM/ATHENS – Israel and Greece signed a €3 billion (S$4.43 billion) defence deal on Aug 31 under which Israel will build a multi-layered air defence system for Greece as Athens pushes ahead with a broader military modernisation programme.
Israel’s defence ministry said it was Israel’s largest-ever defence export deal with Greece and one of the biggest in the country’s history. The agreement confirmed an earlier Reuters report.
Amir Baram, director-general of Israel’s defence ministry, said the so-called Achilles Shield deal reflected “Israel’s technological edge and the proven track record of our defence systems in the field”.
Under the deal, Israel will supply Greece with the David’s Sling and SPYDER systems produced by Rafael Advanced Defense Systems and the BARAK MX system made by Israel Aerospace Industries, as well as MMR multi-mission radars for air surveillance, manufactured by IAI unit ELTA Systems.
David’s Sling was used by Israel to intercept Iranian missiles during the war with Iran in 2026. Greece becomes the second customer for the system after Finland.
Greece spends nearly 3.5 per cent of its gross domestic product on defence, a higher proportion than many NATO allies due to its long-standing dispute with neighbouring Turkey.
Athens plans to spend about €28 billion by 2036 to build the Achilles Shield multi-layer anti-ballistic, anti-aircraft and anti-drone system, and to buy up to 40 F-35 fighter jets from the US and frigates from France and Italy.
Under the deal on Aug 31, Greece will receive a new national command-and-control system, developed by Rafael, to integrate the country’s air-defence capabilities.
A supplementary €26 million agreement will see Israel supply Greece with Rafael’s Drone Dome systems to protect strategic sites against drones and reinforce existing defences.
Israel will also expand defence-industrial cooperation with Greece, including transfers of technology and expertise to local industry. REUTERS

A small piece of architecture that connects local building traditions with collective use
name: backdirwas_5 designer: Studio Carraldo author site:Studio Carraldo
The oven stands on a solid concrete base cast using formwork made from round timber logs sourced from the surrounding forests. This construction refers to the traditional log building techniques found in the nearby farmhouses, translating their character into a contemporary architectural language. The oven’s combustion chamber is formed as a dome of refractory firebricks. The dome stores the heat generated during firing and reflects it back into the interior of the oven, allowing the heat to be retained and used efficiently. The structure is enclosed by a sculptural stainless steel body. At the front, the body continues the width of the concrete base, while its sides taper upwards. A horizontal drip edge forms the upper termination of the oven. The wooden shingles widely used throughout the Alpine region are reinterpreted as large stainless steel panels. Connected through an interlocking system, the individual elements come together to form a precisely assembled outer shell. A small piece of architecture that connects local building traditions with collective use. By: Studio Carraldo | @studio.carraldo Design Team: Valentin Fick, Franka Ruhnau, David Zauels Photographer: Studio Carraldo Edits: Jonas Zauels | @blackbvrds

Malaysia’s air quality turns hazardous as Indonesian wildfires burn
Pollution index hits 476 near the border, forcing school closures and triggering emergency cloud-seeding plans in Sarawak
3-MIN READ3-MIN
 Listen
Air pollution in Malaysia’s Bornean state of Sarawak has surged into hazardous territory, with the air pollutant index (API) topping 400 in the worst-hit district, as forest fires raging in Indonesia continue to send thick smoke drifting across the border.
Serian in Sarawak, closest to the frontier with Indonesia’s West Kalimantan province, recorded the highest reading of 476 as of Monday morning.
Kuching, Samarahan and Sri Aman all logged readings above 300 as of 10am, according to Malaysia’s Environment Department.
The API scale classifies anything above 300 as hazardous; readings of 201-300 are “very unhealthy”, 101-200 “unhealthy”, 51-100 “moderate” and 0-50 “good”.
Malaysia has activated its National Open Burning Action Plan and National Haze Action Plan in response, mobilising government agencies to tackle both the fires and the health risks posed by the smoke.

One Dead, 15 People Unaccounted For After Flash Flooding at the Grand Canyon
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-31
07:05:30 UTC
16:05:30 KST

Two people have died and more than a dozen others are missing or unaccounted for after a flash flood ripped through the Grand Canyon over the weekend, according to park service officials.
The National Park Service (NPS) wrote in a social media post on Monday that two bodies have been recovered, with search and rescue efforts ongoing. The NPS earlier shared late Sunday night that rescuers had found the body of a 46-year-old man near Crystal Rapids along the Colorado River. It has not provided any further information about the deceased.
Read More: Nepal Flash Flooding Leaves Hundreds Dead
In a separate statement on Sunday, the agency asked the public for information on 15 individuals who may be missing or remain unaccounted for. As of Sunday morning, 62 people had been evacuated from Phantom Ranch and the lower North Kaibab Trail, and more were expected to be evacuated in nearby areas, NPS officials added.
NPS asked those who know of hikers or backpackers in the inner canyon along the Bright Angel Creek corridor on Saturday, “as well as anyone who had a campground reservation in the affected corridor,” to provide information.
The continuing search may be impacted by rain and thunderstorms that have been forecasted in the area, the agency warned on Monday.
How the Grand Canyon flash flooding unfolded
The flash-flood event occurred in Bright Angel Canyon and the Phantom Ranch area on Saturday afternoon at around 2:30 p.m. Arizona is currently in the throes of the monsoon season, and storms poured over the Grand Canyon from early Saturday morning and returned in the evening.
Nearly all footbridges over Bright Angel Creek were destroyed in the floods, the Park Service said, preventing hikers from crossing. NPS is continuing to assess the extent of the damage. Parts of the canyon—Phantom Ranch, Bright Angel Campground, the Phantom Ranch Canteen and cabins, and the entire North Kaibab Trail from the North Kaibab Trailhead to Phantom Ranch—were closed until further notice.
The Transcanyon Waterline, a 12.5-mile pipeline in the Grand Canyon that carries water for drinking and fire suppression has also been damaged. With that pipeline out of action, the park has a limited water supply and has resorted to conservation measures.
The National Park Service warns of ongoing risk
Other restrictions have been imposed following the floods. By Monday, all concessions inside the park will end overnight accommodations. Only dry camping—camping without utility hookups to water or sewage—will be allowed on the South Rim, and fires on the South Rim and inner canyon areas will be prohibited.
NPS also warned that flash floods may recur and cause debris flow, as thunderstorms and heavy rainfall are anticipated until Monday.
The National Weather Service in Flagstaff, Ariz. has issued a flash flood watch, urging caution in flood-prone areas like creeks, slot canyons, and low water crossings, among others.

China’s 6 biggest state banks post rare shared growth as margins show tentative rebound

Unknown Publisher
2026-08-31

Advertisement
China’s 6 biggest state banks post rare shared growth as margins show tentative rebound
Half-year results rise across China’s largest state-owned lenders amid tentative signs of margin stabilisation
3-MIN READ3-MIN
 Listen
China’s six largest state-owned banks recorded their first simultaneous rise in first-half revenue and net profit since 2022, according to interim results released last week, as margins that had been under pressure for two years showed tentative signs of stabilising.
Industrial and Commercial Bank of China (ICBC), China Construction Bank (CCB), Agricultural Bank of China (ABC), Bank of China (BOC), Bank of Communications (Bocom) and Postal Savings Bank of China (PSBC) together generated more than 2 trillion yuan (US$297 billion) in operating income for the first half.
Combined net profit attributable to shareholders amounted to about 712.6 billion yuan. Revenue grew between 4 and 11 per cent across the six lenders, while net profit rose 4 to 6 per cent – the first time since 2022 that all six registered positive growth on both counts at the same time.
The improvement was underpinned by a tentative rebound in net interest margin (NIM) – the spread between what banks earn on loans and pay on deposits – after two years of steady compression that dragged the industry average down to a record low of nearly 1.4 per cent in the first quarter.
CCB led the turn, posting a half-year NIM of 1.37 per cent – up 0.03 percentage points from full-year 2025 and 0.01 percentage points from the first quarter.

Sadhguru pledges Rs 1 crore for Nepal flood relief, seeks joint Himalayan response
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-31
06:59:19 UTC
15:59:19 KST

Edited by: Vivek Dubey / TIMESOFINDIA.COM / Aug 31, 2026, 12:29 IST

Sadhguru called for a collective approach to managing disasters and protecting the Himalayan ecosystem
Sadhguru Jagadish Vasudev has pledged Rs 1 crore towards Nepal’s Prime Minister Disaster Relief Fund to support rescue and relief efforts following devastating flash floods along the Nepal-Tibet border. He also called for greater cooperation among Himalayan nations, proposing a five-nation Himalayan Board to coordinate responses to disasters affecting the fragile mountain region.Sadhguru made the remarks on Sunday while addressing an event titled “In Solidarity With Nepal” in Kathmandu, his first public appearance since the disaster. According to an official statement by the Isha Foundation, the event brought together people in Kathmandu to express solidarity with those affected.The National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority (NDRRMA) said the death toll from the flash floods has risen to 903, while thousands remain missing.Among those still unaccounted for are 77 participants of the Isha Sacred Walks Kailash Sojourn. The group was at the Gyirong immigration centre on the China side of the border when the disaster struck. Three Isha volunteers stationed on the Nepal side are also missing, according to the foundation.
The Isha Foundation, founded by Sadhguru, organises Kailash Mansarovar pilgrimages each season. Pilgrims travel from Kathmandu through Nepal to Tibet, with trekking on foot forming part of the journey. Sadhguru calls for Himalayan BoardAlongside his financial support for Nepal’s relief efforts, Sadhguru called for a collective approach to managing disasters and protecting the Himalayan ecosystem. He proposed a five-nation Himalayan Board comprising India, China, Pakistan, Nepal and Bhutan.Arguing that the Himalayan mountain system cuts across political boundaries, Sadhguru said countries sharing the range needed to coordinate their actions."The mountains don't know your political affiliation. The mountains don't know what nonsense or language you speak. Even if you cannot administer it as one body, at least consultation must happen as one body. There must be some congruence of action in what we do because the Himalayas are the most fantastic and majestic feature on the planet. At the same time, they are very fragile," Sadhguru asserted.He called for the proposed body to be established urgently, saying the Himalayas needed to be treated as a shared natural system rather than as separate national concerns."A body comprising all these nations where the Himalayan ranges run has to happen now. Even if political administrations are separate, the mountain ranges have to be looked at as a feature that needs to be protected for future generations on the planet.
If we don't do this and go on thinking, okay, it's Nepal's problem, let them deal with their problem, there will never be a solution."Sadhguru also said the scale of the disaster was beyond what could reasonably have been anticipated and argued that Nepal could not be expected to deal with its aftermath alone."Nobody expected something like this to happen, that three-fourths of a glacial ice cube will just fall down four thousand feet down the peak. Not something anybody calculates it for. But now that it's happened, we must look at this because this is not something a small nation like Nepal can solve by themselves," Sadhguru said.

Japan begins 23rd release of Fukushima nuclear-contaminated wastewater into ocean
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-31
14:39:21 CST
15:39:21 KST

TOKYO, Aug. 31 (Xinhua) -- Japan on Monday kicked off a new round of discharge of nuclear-contaminated wastewater from the crippled Fukushima Daiichi Nuclear Power Plant into the sea, marking the 23rd such release since the controversial operation began in 2023.
The discharge started at 11:29 a.m. local time. According to the plant's operator, Tokyo Electric Power Company Holdings (TEPCO), about 7,800 tonnes of wastewater containing approximately 1.2 trillion becquerels of radioactive tritium will be released into the ocean.
The latest discharge, also the fifth round in fiscal 2026, is scheduled to continue through Sept. 18.
In August 2023, Japan unilaterally launched the discharge of nuclear-contaminated water from the Fukushima Daiichi plant into the ocean despite concerns and opposition from the international community. Aug. 24 this year marked three years since the controversial operation began, with a cumulative total of approximately 173,000 tonnes of wastewater released to date.
According to data from TEPCO, as of Aug. 13, storage tanks at the Fukushima Daiichi plant still held about 1.235 million tonnes of nuclear-contaminated water. ■

Across China: China builds pest radar network to protect grain crops
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-31
14:38:58 CST
15:38:58 KST

BEIJING, Aug. 31 (Xinhua) -- A network of insect-tracking radars is being expanded across China to help farmers battle migratory pests that threaten the country's food supply.
In east China's Zhejiang Province, a key migration corridor where northern and southern rice-growing regions meet, a radar station operates at the edge of a paddy field. When a small pest flies past, the system can capture its size, weight and other identifying data.
One target is the rice plant hopper, a migratory insect weighing just 1 milligram and measuring a few millimeters long. It pierces rice stalks and sucks out sap.
During a demonstration test, technicians flew a drone carrying only one rice plant hopper about 300 meters from the radar. Moments later, a monitoring screen displayed the pest's body length, width and weight. Such milligram-level measurements can now be achieved with precision, said Liu Dazhong, an associate researcher at Zhejiang-based Xianghu Laboratory, which monitors major migratory pests. "It has placed us at the forefront globally," Liu noted.
This tiny pest can pose a substantial threat. Of the 11 pests on China's list of first-class agricultural pests, eight can ride seasonal winds and travel more than 100 km overnight across regions. From 2021 to 2024, these eight pests infested an average of 83 million hectares of grain fields annually, accounting for 40 percent of all pest-related damage to the country's rice, wheat and corn, according to the National Agro-Tech Extension and Service Center.
Wu Kongming, an academician at the Chinese Academy of Engineering, said a single adult migratory pest can produce over 1,000 offspring. "The offspring of one adult pest can reduce yields by one-third or even more," he noted.
Outer winds from recent typhoons have accelerated pest migration into the region this month, while high field humidity has created favorable conditions for rapid plant hopper breeding. The pressure on pest and disease control has, as a result, increased greatly in this area recently. Scientists warn that once pest numbers get too high, rice plants will turn yellow and fall over. In severe cases, it may lead to total crop failure.
Rice grower Sheng Yunxiong, based in central China's Hubei Province, said he had rarely seen so many plant hoppers in previous years, but their numbers surged suddenly this August. "I followed the guidance from agricultural technicians and applied pesticide in time. The infestation is now under control," he said. He added that many farmers used to mistakenly believe that rice near maturity did not need pest protection.
Chinese research teams have developed multiple types of insect radars that now provide real-time data on where pests originate, their numbers and their trajectory. The system moves the warning window from "detection after arrival" to "alert before landing," giving farmers 24 to 48 hours of advance notice, a critical period for coordinated control efforts.
Across the country, 65 insect radars are now connected to a national monitoring platform. By 2030, the network is expected to exceed 150 radars, covering all primary migration corridors and eliminating blind spots in core farming areas.
It will form a three-tier defense: radar-based high-altitude monitoring, aerial interception of adult insects and precise ground trapping.
Moreover, migratory pests are a global problem. For example, the fall armyworm, a pest native to the tropical and subtropical regions of the Americas, has devastated maize and other staple crops across Africa since its arrival in 2016. In January 2019, the fall armyworm migrated from Myanmar into southwest China's Yunnan Province, and quickly spread to 18 provincial-level regions. Such threats make international cooperation essential.
China has, notably, shared its tech expertise in cross-border migratory pest control with other Asian countries including Laos, Vietnam and Kazakhstan, via the United Nations Food and Agriculture Organization's South-South cooperation programs. ■

103 years on, Chinese victims of 1923 earthquake massacre commemorated in Japan
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-31
14:38:44 CST
15:38:44 KST

TOKYO, Aug. 31 (Xinhua) -- Chinese laborers and students who were killed in a massacre in Japan after the 1923 Great Kanto Earthquake were remembered at memorial events in Tokyo on Sunday, with participants calling on the Japanese government to squarely confront the country's history as a perpetrator.
This year marks the 103rd anniversary of the atrocity. On Sunday morning, a group of people gathered at Sakasai Bridge in Tokyo's Koto Ward to commemorate Wang Xitian, a leader of Chinese workers in Japan who was killed by Japanese soldiers during the massacre.
Wang was born in 1896 in Changchun City of northeast China's Jilin Province. In 1922, he founded and served as the chairman of the "mutual aid association of Chinese workers in Japan," dedicating himself to assistance work for Chinese laborers and confronting the Japanese government on their behalf.
Following the 1923 Great Kanto Earthquake, Wang was killed by the Japanese military while working to help Chinese laborers and investigate the truth behind the massacre. He was only 27 at the time of his death.
Naoyuki Maniwa, a member of the Koto City Assembly, said, "Each of us bears responsibility for our own country's history. As a politician, it is absolutely unacceptable to show no reflection on the mistakes our country has made and the harm it has inflicted in the past."
In the afternoon, another memorial ceremony for the Chinese victims of the massacre was held at the Higashi-ojima Culture Center.
Speaking at the event, Zhou Chunhua and Zhou Songquan, descendants of Chinese victims, said efforts must continue to uncover the truth of this chapter of history and pursue fairness and justice. They also called on the Japanese government to confront historical crimes and responsibility.
Japanese political figures including Mizuho Fukushima, leader of Japan's Social Democratic Party, and Yoshifu Arita, a member of the House of Representatives, sent written messages to the event. They said Japan should face its history squarely, eliminate discrimination and xenophobia, and prevent tragedies from happening again.
On Sept. 1, 1923, a 7.9-magnitude earthquake struck Japan's Kanto area, resulting in over 140,000 casualties. In the ensuing chaos, Japanese militarist mobs fanned xenophobic sentiment and fabricated pretexts to incite violence against Chinese and Korean laborers. Over 750 Chinese laborers and students, as well as more than 6,000 Korean laborers living in Japan, were brutally killed.
In 1924, Japanese authorities formulated a compensation plan for the victims of the massacre, but it remains unfulfilled to date. ■

Severe late-August wildfires across northern Algeria have brought residential areas, agricultural lands, and critical transport corridors directly into the path of rapidly spreading flames. The destruction across Jijel, Béjaïa, and Tizi Ouzou claimed at least 12 lives and forced the emergency closure of major national highways. The latest outbreak follows a summer of repeated fires across the country, with authorities recorded nearly 2,000 fires nationwide in July, while fires in the northeastern province of Annaba at the end of the month forced more than 100 people to leave their homes and damaged nearly 150 houses. The current fires have again brought residential areas, roads and other infrastructure into the path of rapidly spreading flames. Forest fires occur regularly in northern Algeria during the summer, with increasingly frequent drought and periods of intense heat contributing to more severe fire conditions.
The situation in Algeria forms part of a wider 2026 wildfire season affecting communities across multiple continents. As of August 1, 112.3 million hectares had burned globally, according to data from the Global Wildfire Information System compiled by Our World in Data. Africa accounted for 55.1 percent of the total burned area, with the Democratic Republic of Congo recording the largest national total at 13.6 million hectares, followed by Australia at 11.8 million hectares and Angola at 7.5 million hectares. The figures include agricultural and prescribed burning, meaning they do not directly represent the extent of uncontrolled wildfires.
According to the European Forest Fire Information System (EFFIS), 634,473 hectares had burned across the European Union by August 27 in fires larger than 30 hectares. Although the figure remains below the 984,559 hectares recorded during the same period in 2025, it is more than twice the 2006-2025 average of 313,246 hectares. EFFIS forecasts very extreme conditions in isolated areas across central Europe and the Balkans, as well as Portugal, eastern Spain and the Atlas Mountains of North Africa, with extreme danger extending through parts of southeastern Europe and toward Ukraine. The forecast for August 31 to September 6 also indicates above-average temperatures across the Iberian Peninsula and North Africa, while below-average rainfall is expected in parts of the Iberian Peninsula, France, Italy and the Balkans.

Spain has experienced one of the most severe fire seasons in Europe this year, with approximately 226,391 hectares burned by August 1. France has also faced major fires, while simultaneous fires in the two countries have led to mass evacuations. In the United Kingdom, fires have affected areas including the Cairngorms, while elsewhere in Europe, communities have faced smoke, evacuations and damage to homes and infrastructure. The impacts extend beyond Europe and North Africa. Canada had recorded approximately 2 million hectares burned by August 1, with fires across several provinces forcing communities to evacuate and sending smoke into parts of Canada and the United States. The United States had recorded approximately 2.4 million hectares burned, with major fires reported in Oregon, Washington and Idaho. Australia recorded approximately 11.8 million hectares burned during the same period.
The scale and geographic spread of this year's fires are unfolding alongside increasingly hot and dry conditions associated with climate change. The combination of higher temperatures, drought and dry vegetation can create conditions that allow fires to spread more rapidly and become harder to contain. At the same time, the immediate impacts remain highly local: homes are evacuated, roads are closed, landscapes are burned and communities face the difficult process of returning and rebuilding. For the built environment, the consequences of the current fire season are particularly visible where fires reach settlements. Homes can be damaged or destroyed alongside roads and other infrastructure, while evacuations can rapidly turn ordinary streets and highways into critical emergency routes. In Algeria, the closure of three national highways demonstrates how wildfire can disrupt regional connectivity in addition to threatening individual properties.
Across different regions, extreme weather and seismic events have caused significant loss of life and damage to communities in recent weeks. On August 26, a glacier collapse triggered flash floods along the Nepal–Tibet border, destroying villages and leaving at least 350 people dead and more than 1,300 missing, with the most affected areas including Nepal's Rasuwa and Nuwakot districts. Earlier this month, a magnitude 7.4 earthquake struck Colombia, causing damage across several cities and killing at least 111 people. The event followed four significant earthquakes in Japan, the United States, and Venezuela within a 36-hour period in June, highlighting the range of environmental risks currently affecting communities and the built environment.

disposable retail price tags are reimagined as copper and enamel pins
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-31
06:15:33 UTC
15:15:33 KST

retail price labels become collectible copper and enamel pins
Precious Price Tag Pins transforms the familiar price label, an everyday symbol of consumer culture, into a series of wearable and collectible objects. Following her viral project Oyster card acrylic nails, artist Lucie Davis’ new work examines how value can be reassigned to an overlooked object through material transformation, repetition, and craft.
The series combines laser engraving with traditional hand enameling, bringing together digital precision and kiln-fired finishing techniques. Each pin begins as a metal cutout that is laser engraved with the graphic details of a price label before being finished with vitreous enamel. The pieces are fired in a kiln to produce a glossy, permanent surface, with variations in temperature and firing time deliberately introduced during the process.
The firing experiments included under-firing and over-firing individual pieces to observe how changes in temperature affected the enamel surface. These variations produce differences in color, texture, and finish, with some outcomes occurring through the unpredictability of the kiln. Before firing, the corners of the copper cutouts are hammered to create small deformations that suggest the appearance of a sticker beginning to peel away from a surface.
each pin preserves the imperfections of the original price label
The project grew out of designer Lucie Davis’s familiarity with retail price labels while working in a shop during university. Repeated exposure to the stickers drew attention to their printing marks, creases, bends, and other traces of handling. The series collects and reproduces these details as part of the design, transferring the visual characteristics of disposable retail labels into more permanent objects.
Each pin is made from copper with laser-engraved, kiln-fired enamel and is fitted with a tie tack pin and silver clasp. Variations in the engraving, metal deformation, and firing process mean that no two pieces are identical. The resulting differences give each object a distinct surface and appearance while retaining the visual language of the original price label.
The pins can be worn individually as jewelry or displayed together as a collection. When grouped, their repetition and accumulation reference the mass-produced stickers from which the series takes its form, while the transformation into enamel and copper objects introduces a different form of material and monetary value.

The plea sought ethanol-content labelling at pumps and on bills, a vehicle-wise E20 compatibility database, an expert review of its impact, and a transition plan for incompatible vehicles.
NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Monday refused to entertain a plea seeking mandatory disclosure of the exact ethanol content in petrol at fuel stations and on fuel purchase receipts.A bench of Justices MM Sundresh and PB Varale dismissed the plea filed by advocate Narendra Goswami, while granting him liberty to approach the concerned high court.The Attorney General for India, R Venkataramani, appearing for the Centre, argued that the petition was a proxy litigation, as the court had already dismissed a similar petition on the issue."The petitioner wants government of India to be answerable to him," the AG submitted, as quoted by PTI.Meanwhile, Goswami contended that he has the right to know the content of the petrol given. "Not only me but citizens at large should be informed about the composition of the fuel given to them," he submitted.The plea sought directions to petrol pumps to prominently display the precise percentage of ethanol blended with petrol. It also sought that the ethanol content be specifically mentioned on receipts and invoices issued to consumers at fuel stations and an official vehicle-wise compatibility database covering different ethanol blends, based on factors such as manufacturer, model, engine type and year of manufacture.
"Direct the respondents (Centre and others) to prepare and publish within a stipulated time an official, public, vehicle-wise compatibility database searchable by manufacturer, model, engine type and year of manufacture, indicating the suitability or otherwise of various ethanol blends for each vehicle," Goswami added in his plea.
The plea also called for an independent expert committee, including representatives from the petroleum and road transport ministries, the Bureau of Indian Standards and independent automobile engineers, to assess the real-world compatibility of E20 with existing vehicles.
The committee was also asked to examine the impact of E20 on fuel efficiency, engine life and maintenance costs, warranty and insurance, emissions, water consumption in ethanol production, and food-security concerns.The petitioner further sought a national consumer disclosure protocol for ethanol-blended petrol and a transparent transition framework for older or incompatible vehicles, including the possible availability of lower-ethanol petrol where feasible.

Another Ukrainian town lies in ruins as Russians creep closer
DRUZHKIVKA, Ukraine, Aug 31 - Burned out cars. Rubble from flattened buildings strewn along deserted streets. The rumble of artillery guns followed by the high-pitched whine of an attack drone.
This is today's reality in the eastern Ukrainian town of Druzhkivka, where a handful of civilians eke out a living alongside soldiers fighting the Russians who are now just 15 km (nine miles) away and gradually moving closer.
Such scenes of devastation are being repeated all along the 1,200-km (746-mile) front in the east and south of the country. As Russian forces advance, apartment blocks, markets and shops are razed and towns and villages become virtually uninhabitable.
"I can't sleep," said Iryna Litovchenko, one of a handful of civilians who have stayed. "Some guys took us in - strangers," added the 56-year-old, walking through broken glass and debris beside badly damaged buildings.
"My home is gone, as if it never existed. There were so many good things, so much of everything. In one fell swoop – boom — it's as if nothing's left."
Druzhkivka lies on the road linking strategic towns and cities known as the "fortress belt", a string of urban settlements that Russia is desperate to breach as it tries to seize the whole of Ukraine's eastern Donbas region.
That remains one of Russian President Vladimir Putin's primary objectives in the war, but well over four years after he launched a full-scale invasion, his forces are struggling to break through Ukraine's defences.
'OUR CITY IS GONE'
Litovchenko does not flinch at the loud blast from a nearby howitzer. But when she hears the soft buzz of a drone above, she stops before taking shelter under the branches of a tree.
Thousands of Russian and Ukrainian unmanned aerial vehicles, most steered remotely by pilots, fill the skies close to the front, hunting their prey with deadly efficiency.
In Druzhkivka, and all along the fortress belt, many roads are covered with netting to protect anyone travelling on them from drones. An unmanned ground vehicle, used to supply frontline Ukrainian positions and evacuate wounded soldiers, whizzes towards its next mission.
Zoya, a 63-year-old selling basic food items outside a charred market stall, does not want to leave her home town, despite the dangers.
"I know a bomb could come flying in and I'll die. I understand that perfectly well."
"It's heartbreaking," she added, pointing to the destruction around her. "It makes me want to cry. I was born here, I grew up here. I just don't know. Our city is gone." REUTERS

India, UK Fire Up Defense Cooperation With Joint Development
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-31
06:03:00 UTC
15:03:00 KST

India and the United Kingdom are close to signing two inter-governmental agreements (IGAs) for the incorporation of electric propulsion on Indian Navy ships and production of Marlet lightweight multirole missiles (LMM). These are decisive steps toward forging long-term defense industrial cooperation and deepening the bilateral strategic partnership.
At the same time, the U.K. has also upped its pitch for another mega-deal — the design and development of a jet engine to power the advanced medium combat aircraft (AMCA), India’s fifth-generation fighter.
The two countries have made concerted efforts to deepen defense cooperation and find a long-term overarching deal to anchor that effort. This intent was formalized in the 10‑year Defense Industrial Roadmap under the “Vision 2035” announced last year, which focuses on deepening collaboration in advanced technologies and complex weapons, supporting innovation and co-development, through cooperation programs such as the Jet Engine Advanced Core Technologies. It also calls for strengthening research and development on developing new capabilities, including underwater systems and direct energy weapons.
The expanding military-to-military cooperation, joint exercises and research collaborations add to the broadening cooperation. Another important binding factor is overlapping concerns and converging interests in the Indo-Pacific, where Britain sees India as one of the most important “stabilizing forces.”
Beyond defense and security, the overall relationship too has leapfrogged with high-level commitment from both sides. That push led to the conclusion of the bilateral Free Trade Agreement (FTA), one of the biggest trade deals of modern times, that came into effect on July 15, 2026.
Integrated Full Electric Propulsion (IFEP)
The IGA to be signed is to develop and incorporate IFEP for the Indian Navy’s four landing platform docks (LPD) for which a separate tender is underway. The conversation for deploying IFEP on Indian Navy’s future vessels is several years old, as the Indian Navy set its sights on shifting from diesel to electric propulsion engines to bring in efficiency, and reduce fossil fuel dependency and emissions.
Formalizing the conversation, a joint working group called the “India-UK electric propulsion capability partnership” was set up in early 2023. A Statement of Intent to co-design, co-create and co-produce maritime electric propulsion systems was signed in November 2024, and the intent to finalize an IGA was announced when the India and British prime ministers met in Mumbai in October 2025. As part of the cooperation, GE Vernova and state-owned Bharat Heavy Electricals Limited announced the setting up of India’s first land-based test facility for IFEP.
However, IFEP systems on four LPDs are just the start, as the Indian Navy is targeting a 200-ship force by 2035 in response to expanding Chinese naval numbers and presence in the Indian Ocean Region. Some existing ships could also be converted to electric propulsion. The IFEP brings significant operational efficiencies in this regard, which the Royal Navy has mastered, having operationally deployed it on several frontline ships, including its aircraft carrier. In April 2023, U.K.’s Chief of Defense Staff Admiral Sir Tony Radakin observed that the U.K. is one of the world’s leaders in maritime electric propulsion, having been on it for at least 20 years, and cooperation with the U.K. means that India “doesn’t have to go through a 20-year journey.”
The LPD project, an ambition for almost two decades, received a fresh sanction from the Defense Acquisition Council, the highest body for procurements in India’s Ministry of Defense, in October 2025. These vessels, displacing around 29,000 tons, will be built by Indian shipyards in partnership with foreign partners.
Once rolled out, this deal will intertwine collaboration over the next several decades. However, given India’s notorious procurement process, the IFEP deployment depends on the LPD deal reaching its logical conclusion in a reasonable timeframe.
The Elusive Engine Deal
India is looking for a global partner for design and development of a 120kN jet engine to power the AMCA-Mk2. While negotiations between Safran of France and Gas Turbine Research Establishment (GTRE) have been ongoing for several years now, the delay opened prospects for the U.K’s Rolls Royce and the U.S.’ General Electric. Rolls Royce, which has been working closely with the Indian research establishment for several years, has presented a compelling offer, including full control over Intellectual Property for the engine developed.
On August 14, Rolls Royce announced a partnership with Reliance Industries Limited to explore the formation of a dedicated Aerospace Gas Turbine Complex that will be a center of excellence for power and propulsion technology in India. This significantly ups the ante in support of its offer.
However, some practical realities stand out, which will determine partner selection. For instance, despite assurance that U.S. International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) does not apply to engine collaboration as it’s an IGA, concerns remain in Indian policy circles given Britain’s alliance with the U.S. and possible impact on future deals.
This is particularly so as all the variants of India’s indigenous light combat aircraft and AMCA-Mk1, cumulatively about half the fighter squadron strength in two decades, will be powered by GE engines, a U.S. company. That positions France favorably given its independent arms industry and the trajectory of Indo-French ties. Adding to that is India’s interest in joining the French future combat air system (FCAS), sixth-generation fighter program. If the same engine or its derivative can go into the FCAS, that would be a lucrative proposition both economically and operationally.
Widening Cooperation
Last year, India and the U.K. made several important announcements on the defense front. At Aero India in February 2025, U.K. announced the formal launch of “Defense Partnership–India,” or DP-I, a dedicated cell within the U.K. Ministry of Defense for deepening cooperation.
Several cooperation agreements were also signed at the biennial expo in Bengaluru, including production of Starstreak man portable air defense systems (MANPADS) and LMMs and the establishment of an advanced short-range air to air missile (ASRAAM) assembly and test facility in India.
The two countries also conducted their largest-ever maritime exercise last year that saw their Carrier Strike Groups exercise together. A separate air defense exercise saw the Royal Navy deploying its aircraft to exercise with the Indian Navy and Indian Air Force.
A contract for laser beam riding Starstreak Man-portable air-defense systems or MANPADS was also signed between Thales U.K. and Bharat Dynamics Limited (BDL) under the Emergency Procurement route for 16 launchers, 56 missiles and one simulator worth around $35 million. This could potentially expand to thousands of missiles in future. The two companies had then announced their intent for collaboration to produce LMMs in India. The IGA to be signed soon will make India one of the largest markets for the missiles. Similarly, weapons manufacturer MBDA U.K. and BDL are setting up a first-of-its-kind ASRAAM assembly and test facility in Hyderabad to also cater to exports, after the missile was chosen for the Jaguar and Light Combat Aircraft-Mk1A.
British defense companies like Thales, Rolls Royce and several others have integrated Indian companies into their global supply chains. With the expanding cooperation and an enabling FTA, this is set to significantly expand. With the Indian defense manufacturing ecosystem significantly maturing over the years, it offers scale and capacity, the criticality of which was showcased in the West Asia conflict.
Military-to-military engagements have also expanded. For instance, with agreement early this year on the deployment of three IAF qualified flying instructors to a Royal Air Force training base, Indian officers are now embedded as instructors at all three UK service academies. Britain has also been leveraging the bilateral logistics sharing agreement signed in 2022 to augment its deployments in the Indian Ocean Region. In addition to spares and supplies, under the logistics pact, Royal Navy ships have undergone essential repair at an Indian shipyard during their deployment in the region. Britain was the fifth country to post a liaison officer at the Indian Navy’s Information Fusion Centre for Indian Ocean Region (IFC-IOR) in Gurugram inaugurated in 2018 to promote maritime domain awareness.
The India-U.K. relationship has struggled with several irritants in the past, including Khalistani separatism in the U.K, and Britain’s ties with Pakistan. However, there is determination on both sides to expand ties amid geopolitical uncertainties and a changing world order.
With this slew of agreements, Britain is looking to regain lost space in India’s growing defense sector. For India, the U.K is one of the important stabilizing vectors in its multilateral alignment strategy to safeguard its interests.

Taiwan expands NHI drug coverage, IVF subsidies and children’s dental care
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-31
05:49:09 UTC
14:49:09 KST

TAIPEI (Taiwan News) — The National Health Insurance Administration will expand coverage for cholesterol-lowering drugs and add treatments for rare diseases beginning Sept. 1, while the government will also increase subsidies for in vitro fertilization and expand dental fluoride treatment for children, per UDN.
The NHIA said the changes to reimbursement rules for cholesterol-lowering drugs are intended to bring coverage in line with the “2025 Taiwan Lipid Management Clinical Pathway Consensus.” The expanded coverage will apply to statins, ezetimibe, and combination drugs with eligibility determined according to patients' cardiovascular risk levels and LDL-C treatment thresholds.
The agency estimates the changes will benefit about 1.05 million additional patients and increase annual drug spending by approximately NT$2.28 billion. The agency said the changes are intended to allow patients with high cholesterol to receive appropriate medication earlier and reduce their risk of cardiovascular disease.
The NHIA will also add two drugs for rare diseases to its reimbursement program. Fabhalta 200mg hard capsules, containing iptacopan, will be covered for eligible adult patients with paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria, or PNH. As an oral treatment, the drug provides another treatment option for patients with the rare blood disorder.
Livmarli oral solution, containing maralixibat chloride, will also receive temporary NHI coverage for eligible patients aged 1 and older with progressive familial intrahepatic cholestasis and Alagille syndrome (ALGS) who experience severe itching. The agency formally announced the temporary reimbursement of Livmarli on Aug. 14.
The government will also expand free fluoride treatment for children. Under the revised program, children will be eligible for subsidized fluoride treatment from birth through Aug. 31 of the year they enter elementary school. The change addresses a gap under the previous age rules that left some children who were already six but had not yet entered elementary school ineligible for the service.
The service includes professional fluoride treatment by dentists, oral examinations, and oral health education covering proper tooth cleaning, healthy eating, and other preventive measures.
Before entering elementary school, children can receive subsidized treatment every six months. Disadvantaged children younger than 12 from low-income households, as well as children with disabilities and those living in Indigenous, remote, or outlying island areas, can receive treatment every three months. The government estimates the expanded eligibility will benefit about 128,000 additional children, per UDN.
The Health Ministry said the prevalence of cavities in baby teeth among 5-year-olds fell from 65.4% in 2018 to 46.3%, while the average number of decayed, missing, or filled permanent teeth among 12-year-old students declined from 3.31 in 2000 to 2.01 in 2020.
The government will also increase subsidies for IVF treatment beginning Sept. 1. Under the revised IVF 3.0 program, the maximum subsidy for the second and third treatment cycles for each pregnancy will increase from NT$100,000 to NT$150,000 for women younger than 40.
For women aged 40 to under 45, the maximum subsidy for the second and third cycles will increase from NT$80,000 to NT$130,000. The Health Promotion Administration said the higher subsidies apply to applications submitted beginning Sept. 1.
The HPA estimates that about 20,000 people currently receive IVF subsidies each year and that the expanded program will provide higher subsidies to nearly 5,000 women.

TSMC sees silicon photonics gaining momentum in 2027
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-31
05:48:23 UTC
14:48:23 KST

TAIPEI (Taiwan News) — TSMC Vice President Hsu Kuo-chin (徐國晉) said Monday that silicon photonics is gaining momentum as AI workloads push data center networks toward their physical and power limits.
Hsu said at a silicon photonics forum that silicon photonics could account for more than 50% of the optical transceiver market in 2027, per Liberty Times. He said some companies are expected to begin mass production of co-packaged optics (CPO) products in the second half of this year.
Hsu said AI is creating not only software challenges but also physical and power constraints as data centers handle rapidly increasing computing workloads. Optical transceivers are becoming important to data center infrastructure, with global sales rising 25% in 2025 and projected to increase another 50% this year, he said.
Demand for higher-speed products is also accelerating, per CNA. Sales of optical transceivers supporting speeds of 100G and above doubled in 2024 and increased another 60% in 2025, Hsu said.
Hsu said Taiwan's semiconductor foundry ecosystem can produce optical engines at scale and with high precision, making CPO the ultimate application of silicon photonics. He said concerns over CPO have eased as real-world data and market validation have accumulated.
The semiconductor industry has broadly embraced silicon photonics, Hsu said, but scaling up the technology will require progress across other parts of the supply chain, including lasers, fiber-optic connectors, and testing.

Mexico's trade ties with U.S. pose biggest challenge of century: economy minister
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-31
13:45:28 CST
14:45:28 KST

MEXICO CITY, Aug. 30 (Xinhua) -- Mexico's new trade relationship with the United States represents the country's "biggest challenge" so far this century, Economy Minister Marcelo Ebrard said Sunday.
"We have never faced a challenge of this scale and complexity with the United States," Ebrard said during a meeting of the ruling National Regeneration Movement party, or Morena, in the Chamber of Deputies.
He said the global economy is undergoing a major shift from a free trade-based system to one increasingly shaped by protectionist principles aimed at bringing some manufacturing back to the United States.
Under the new changes, Ebrard said, where a product is made is increasingly important, whereas price and quality, particularly price, used to matter more.
In this context, Mexico has sought to preserve access to the U.S. market and maintain one of the world's lowest effective tariff rates, he added.
Ebrard said Mexican exports of electronics, computing equipment and products linked to the artificial intelligence boom in the United States rose sharply between 2025 and 2026.
Mexico's government expects the economy to grow between 1.8 percent and 2.8 percent this year.
Mexico's economy, the second largest in Latin America after Brazil, expanded 0.5 percent in 2025, driven mainly by services amid weakness in industrial activity linked to the United States. ■

14:45:06 KST

WELLINGTON, Aug. 31 (Xinhua) -- The New Zealand government has canceled a planned fuel excise hike for 2027 to help ease cost-of-living pressures while delivering lower taxes for New Zealanders, senior officials said on Monday.
A 12 cents-per-liter increase scheduled for Jan. 1, 2027 would be scrapped. The next increase of 5 cents per liter will instead take effect on Jan. 1, 2028, with three further 5-cent increases at six-month intervals. Equivalent increases to road user charges will also be delayed until 2028, Transport Minister Chris Bishop told a press conference.
"Canceling next year's fuel excise increase and spreading the change over time from 2028 will give Kiwis more time to recover from the period of post-COVID economic pain and recent uncertainty in the Middle East," Finance Minister Nicola Willis said in a statement.
Bishop said transport project costs had risen by as much as 45 percent since 2020, while fuel excise had remained frozen and fallen about 20 percent in real terms.
The government will top up the National Land Transport Fund to offset lost fuel excise revenue, at an expected cost of 1.476 billion NZ dollars (about 870 million U.S. dollars) over the forecast period, he said.
The cost will be partly offset by a 450-million-NZ-dollar fuel response contingency established through Budget 2026, according to the government. ■

Demand for dog DNA tests surges after Hong Kong clampdown over attacks
Animal welfare groups also warn that the government’s response to a string of dog attacks could lead to a wave of pet abandonments
A government clampdown following a spate of dog attacks in Hong Kong has sparked a rush for canine DNA testing, while animal welfare groups warn the aggressive enforcement could trigger a wave of pet abandonments.
Amid mounting public backlash over the sudden seizure and impounding of suspected fighting dogs, an advocacy group on Monday urged authorities to introduce a one-year grace period for owners to voluntarily declare pets with fighting-breed traits.
The incident exposed major loopholes in the city’s self-declaration microchip registration system, after the animal was found to carry genetic traits of the pit bull terrier – one of four fighting breeds strictly banned from import and unauthorised breeding in Hong Kong.
As panic spread among dog owners, commercial testing centres saw a surge in clients seeking genetic proof to prevent their pets from being impounded.
Clement Lai Yat-lung, founder of pet testing firm Hero DNA, said inquiries had surged more than fivefold over the past week, jumping from about 10 to between 50 and 60.

Trump posts AI video of Iran's Kharg in 'smithereens', no evidence of attack
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-31
05:40:36 UTC
14:40:36 KST

Iran dismisses Trump's post of attack on key energy hub of Kharg
DUBAI, Aug 31 - An Iranian official dismissed as "laughable" on Monday a post by Donald Trump of an AI-generated video clip that the U.S. president said showed Iran's oil hub Kharg Island being "blown to smithereens".
Hours after Sunday's post, there was no evidence Kharg had been attacked. The White House and the U.S. Defense Department did not immediately respond to Reuters requests for comment outside regular business hours.
Trump's post came shortly after the U.S. and Iran resumed hostilities for the first time since late July, further denting hopes for any early resolution of a conflict now in its sixth month and driving oil prices nearly 2% higher on Monday.
U.S. forces on Sunday struck two Iranian launchers on Iran's Larak Island, some 660 km (410 miles) east of Kharg, a U.S. official said, prompting Iran to retaliate by attacking two U.S. bases in Jordan, according to Iranian media.
"Kharg Island being blown to smithereens!!! President DJT," Trump had said on his Truth Social platform on Sunday, with no further details.
Reuters confirmed that an accompanying video clip showing dramatic explosions was most likely synthetically generated, using software that detects AI-manipulated imagery.
"Trump’s tweets are laughable and conditions in Kharg are calm and appropriate," Hamid Bovard, chief executive of government-run National Iranian Oil Co, said on Monday.
Oil operations have not stopped and workers were busy repairing previous damage and modernising facilities, he added in comments cited by Nournews, a semi-official outlet close to Iran's top security body.
IRAN VOWS TO RESPOND TO ANY ATTACKS
Kharg handled 90% of Iran's oil exports before the war launched by U.S. and Israeli attacks on February 28, and attacking it would severely disrupt energy trade and put huge pressure on the economy.
Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said his country was not seeking war but would respond decisively to any aggression.
"We will never remain silent in the face of any aggression...," state media quoted him as saying on Monday ahead of a visit to Kyrgyzstan.
It was not clear if he was speaking before or after Trump's post on Kharg Island.
A U.S. official said forces had attacked the Iranian launchers on Larak Island on Sunday after "Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps forces were observed preparing to launch rockets with sea mines into the Strait of Hormuz".
Larak is a small island in the strait near the strategic Iranian port of Bandar Abbas. The strait, which normally handles a fifth of global crude oil and liquefied natural gas shipments, has been effectively blocked since the start of the war.
In a statement, the U.S. Central Command said it took "limited, precise" action against minelaying forces of Iran's Revolutionary Guards that posed an "imminent threat" in the strait. It gave no details.
In retaliation, as well as attacking the U.S. bases in Jordan, Iran's army said it had also struck the Al Minhad air base in the United Arab Emirates early on Monday. However, the UAE's defence ministry dismissed that report as false.
The UAE defence ministry later said its air force engaged a drone that had come from Iran over its territorial waters. It provided no further details, including whether it was shot down.
The Jordan strikes targeted U.S. bases used to launch and support the attack on Larak, Iran's foreign ministry said.
The Revolutionary Guards used air defence missiles to shoot down a U.S. drone that crashed in Gulf waters, the Mehr news agency said on Monday, citing a statement from the elite force.
A supertanker caught fire and was brought to a complete halt after being struck by two naval mines in the southern Strait of Hormuz, Iran state TV said, citing a Guards' statement.
UAE presidential adviser Anwar Gargash said Iran's policy of targeting Gulf Arab states and Jordan had failed.
"A state of neither war nor peace cannot be a sustainable solution," Gargash said in a post on X, adding that realistic political solutions should begin with de-escalation and the restoration of normal shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.
PILING ECONOMIC PRESSURE ON IRAN
Trump has yet to achieve the objectives he set out at the start of the war: dismantling Iran's nuclear programme, curbing its ability to attack regional rivals and creating conditions for Iranians to overthrow their clerical rulers.
Sunday's return to hostilities followed weeks in which his administration has stepped up efforts to punish Tehran and its business partners with costly economic sanctions, shifting away from military options.
U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent told Reuters on Sunday new secondary sanctions were likely to be unveiled weekly in the effort to pressure Iran, with an initial focus on banks.
Amid threats to shipping, the number of visible commodity vessels transiting the Strait of Hormuz dropped to five a day over the weekend, shipping data showed.
The actual number could be higher as some vessels have switched off automatic identification systems to evade attacks.
The Guards said the supertanker on fire after being hit by mines had been attempting to pass through the waterway illegally, but gave no details of the vessel or crew, according to a statement cited by state television.
Last week, Trump said all mines had been detonated or removed from the international waters of the strait and Iran had been warned that any vessel placing new mines would be destroyed. Iran denied Trump's assertion. REUTERS
